history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row duplicates seq 938 (id thiruparankundram-murugan-temple-madurai), the same Thiruparankundram Subramaniya Swamy temple under the alternate spelling "Thirupparamkunram". The first of Murugan's six sacred abodes (Arupadai Veedu) and a celebrated rock-cut temple. The rock-cut sanctum holds carved shrines of Shiva (as Parangirinathar), Vishnu, Vinayaka, Subramanya and Durga side by side — Shiva and Vishnu facing each other is unusual. Pandya origins (some sources say 6th century AD, others 8th century — verify, disputed); the large pillared mandapams (Aasthaana, Kambathadi, Ardha, Maha) were added by the Nayaks of Madurai (renovations c. 1736). Legend holds that Murugan married Deivanai, daughter of Indra, here after defeating Surapadman, and that he worshipped Shiva here as Parangirinathar. The 150-ft seven-tier Rajagopuram fronts the hill shrine. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists Madurai; the temple is at Thiruparankundram, ~8 km from Madurai city, corrected here.

name: Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple
town_description: Town ~8 km southwest of Madurai at the base of a granite hill, famous as the first of Murugan's six abodes and for the rock-cut Subramaniya Swamy temple; also known for the Murugan-Avvaiyar naval-fruit legend.

travel.railway: Thiruparankundram station (local); Madurai Junction, ~8 km, is the main railhead
travel.road: ~8 km from Madurai city on the Madurai-Kanyakumari road; city buses, autos and taxis

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Karthigai Deepam (deepam lit atop the hill) is the major draw
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM – 1:00 PM, 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM (verify: some sources give 5:00 AM opening)
